a reverse stock split at a ratio of 1-for-50, as the company seeks to regain compliance with the minimum bid price requirement for continued listing of its shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market.

Shareholders approved a reverse stock split at the company's 2026 annual meeting held on June 17, and the company's Class A common stock is expected to begin trading on a 1-for-50 split-adjusted basis on the Nasdaq Global Select Market starting September 11.

If the reverse split had been implemented as of July 31, the total number of outstanding shares would be reduced proportionately from 285,634,650 to 5,712,693, subject to adjustment for fractional shares.

, which closed at $0.26/share on Tuesday, has struggled with a ​severe liquidity crunch, as rising debt and missed ​interest payments have overshadowed progress on its new liquefied natural gas ⁠projects.
